claims.text: All three core artifacts describe the same trip. TRP-00513 appears on the trip record, on the GPS trace and on the fare breakdown, and the trip record's pickup event (started_at 2026-09-01T06:46:40+08:00) matches the trace's first fix at 2026-09-01T06:46:40+08:00. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on matching identifiers and matching pickup time.

The excess is measured on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 51.86 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 38.1 km, an excess of 13.76 km, or 36.1% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass: 13.76 km is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold AND 36.1% is greater than the 20% relative threshold. A route deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trip record's 51.9 km is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not the figure relied on.

The deviation is also MATERIAL: the excess of 13.76 km is greater than the 8.0 km absolute materiality gate in POL-RD-01, which is why the derived deviation status reads 'material'. This is a case in which the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is compulsory, and the finding itself rests on this trip's own trace and nothing else.

The driver's 'jam near Marina so it re-routed me' excuse cannot be run as an exoneration under POL-RD-03. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00513-01, is for the MCE westbound, and the record marks it intersects_route: false - it does not name a road or segment the optimal route traverses, which is the first thing POL-RD-03(a) requires. Its shortest_lawful_alternative_km is null, so the 130% cap in POL-RD-03 cannot even be computed and the leave-the-corridor-and-rejoin test in limb (c) cannot be run. An advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing.

Tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else, as POL-RD-13 requires, the driver's traffic assertion carries no weight. The counterparty statement names no advisory evidence ID; the advisory that is on file carries a validity window overlapping the trip but does not cover the corridor the optimal route uses; and an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08. The measured excess is therefore neither reduced nor replaced by an amended optimal, and the ruling should record that the assertion was discarded and that no advisory covering the optimal corridor was on file.

No other exculpatory route is open on this record. POL-RD-04 fails: the chat log for this trip is empty (message_count 0), so there is no rider instruction, no timestamp and no waypoint_hint or named road to corroborate a requested detour. POL-RD-05 fails: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is nothing to re-quote against. POL-RD-12 fails: vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, and the trip is not pooled. POL-RD-11 fails: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the upfront-fare regime does not govern.

The trace that carries the finding is clean for policy purposes and needs no corroboration. It holds 313 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds - comfortably inside POL-RD-07's 90 second gap limit and its 30 second sustained-interval limit. No POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment arises on this trip, so the deviation may be established on the trace itself and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is available.

Because the deviation is established and no clause excuses it, the refund is arithmetic. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 38.1 + 0.28 x 42.0) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee = 44.935. Refund = charged_total 58.09 - 44.935 = 13.155, which rounds UP to SGD 13.20. That is 22.65% of charged_total, below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.20. There are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines to add or subtract: erp_gantries is empty and the toll/ERP total is 0.00, and no airport surcharge was charged on a trip that ENDS at the airport.

Nothing in the rider's own profile gates or weakens this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) never engages, and in any event that factor may not be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven. The rider's burden is the ordinary one, and it has been met.

The rider does not press the POL-RD-06 uplift, because the record does not support it. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and 0 over completed_trips_90d of 250 is far below the 0.05 ratio, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and the refund stands at the POL-RD-02 figure rather than a POL-RD-06(b) full refund. The materiality of this trip's excess still makes the check compulsory, and the ruling should show it was run.

There is no offsetting driver claim on this record. The fare breakdown's distance_charged_km of 51.9 is not less than the trace's 51.86 km, so the more-than-1.0 km billing shortfall that POL-RD-04 requires before DRIVER_COMPENSATION can be granted does not exist.

The rider's closing remarks about the driver's questions are not carried by any artifact - the chat log for this trip is empty - and the rider does not rest this claim on them. They are assertions citing no evidence ID and are discarded under POL-RD-08; this case is decided on the trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown.

claims.text: The most the rider can recover on this record is SGD 13.20, nowhere near the SGD 58.09 pleaded. Under POL-RD-02 the refund is charged_total less a recomputed fare computed on the OPTIMAL route: charged_total on the fare_breakdown is 58.09, and recomputed_fare is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 38.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 42.0 optimal minutes) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 44.935. Refund before rounding is 13.155, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 13.20. That is 22.6% of the amount charged, far below the 90% that would convert this into a FULL_REFUND, so the ruling is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 13.20 and nothing else.

The rider's pleaded figures ('fifty kilometres somehow became seventy') are not the measured ones, and under POL-RD-01 the governing field is the trace, not the recollection. On EV-GPS-00513 the actual distance is 51.86 km against a booked optimal of 38.1 km, an excess of 13.76 km, or 36.1% — it clears both POL-RD-01 gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and is additionally MATERIAL (over 8.0 km), but it is 13.76 km, not the 20 km the claim asserts. The remedy cannot be inflated by the pleaded number: POL-RD-02's recomputed_fare depends only on optimal_distance_km and optimal_duration_min, never on the actual distance, so no larger deviation yields a larger refund.

The material deviation does trigger the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check, and that check comes back clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither limb of the pattern test is met (0 flags is below the 3-flag limb, and 0/250 = 0.00 is below the 0.05 ratio limb with more than 40 trips). No pattern being established, there is no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c); only the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 13.20 moves. Those two fields are the only ones POL-RD-06 names, and POL-GEN-01 confines the test to them.

Nothing is added to the POL-RD-02 figure for pass-through or statutory lines. The fare_breakdown shows erp_lines totalling 0.00 with no gantry charged, tolls_erp of 0.00, and airport_surcharge of 0.00 — correctly so, because this trip ENDS at Changi and a surcharge on an arriving trip would itself be a billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4). No off-route ERP was charged, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids stacking a pass-through correction on top of the POL-RD-02 refund in any event. The rider's total recovery is therefore SGD 13.20.

The driver's contemporaneous account — a jam near Marina and an app re-route — is corroborated as to the congestion by an independent third-party record: EV-ADVIS-00513-01 (LTA DataMall, ADV-20261413-001) logs slow traffic on the MCE corridor, active 06:16:40 to 08:16:40, overlapping this trip window by 52.0 minutes, which is exactly the Marina-area congestion the driver describes; the driver's profile carries no deviation flags. The driver does not, however, contend that POL-RD-03 exonerates him: that advisory's intersects_route flag is false and shortest_lawful_alternative_km is null, so it neither names a segment the optimal route traverses nor supplies the cap figure POL-RD-03 requires, and under POL-RD-13 an external-traffic assertion is tested against this advisory and nothing else. The excess therefore stands at the measured 13.76 km.

If the tribunal instead treats the driver's POL-RD-03 invocation as live, POL-RD-10(5) is engaged rather than answered: the exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact, EV-ADVIS-00513-01, that lacks the field the clause's cap requires — shortest_lawful_alternative_km is null, so 1.30 x (alternative - optimal) + 1.00 cannot be computed on this record and the record cannot say what part, if any, of the 13.76 km the advisory justifies. On that reading the record does not settle the exoneration question, and the mandatory outcome is ESCALATE: the disputed SGD 58.09 is held rather than collected or refunded while a human reviewer sees the case, the admissibility report and both briefs (POL-GEN-03).

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this concerns trip TRP-00513, Woodlands MRT to Changi Airport Terminal 2, billed at SGD 58.09.

RIDER — your route claim succeeds in part. The driven distance is measured on the governing field, gps_trace.trace_distance_km on EV-GPS-00513: 51.86 km against the booked optimal of 38.1 km on EV-TRIP-00513, an excess of 13.76 km, or 36.1% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. Your pleaded 'fifty kilometres somehow became seventy' is not the measured figure: the excess is 13.76 km, not 20 km, and the refund cannot grow with the pleaded number because POL-RD-02 recomputes only on the optimal route.

The refund is arithmetic. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 38.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 42.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 44.935. Refund = charged_total 58.09 - 44.935 = 13.155, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 13.20. That is 22.6% of the amount charged, well below the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.20. No ERP or toll line was charged (0.00) and no airport surcharge appears (0.00 — correctly, because this trip ENDS at Changi), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and its anti-double-count rule bars stacking any pass-through correction on the POL-RD-02 figure.

DRIVER — your account ('the app showed the CTE-ECP route', 'a jam near Marina so it re-routed me') does not reduce the excess. Under POL-RD-08 an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge your burden, and under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00513-01 covers the wrong corridor (intersects_route is false — the optimal route does not use the MCE westbound) and its shortest_lawful_alternative_km is null, so the POL-RD-03 exoneration and its 130% cap cannot be run; the advisory exonerates nothing and your assertion is discarded. Your advocate's alternative argument that this engages POL-RD-10(5) and forces an escalation is rejected: you named no advisory evidence ID, and POL-RD-13(1) provides that an assertion citing no artifact is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited one. No other escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (313 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, empty gaps, max gap 0 s), the timestamps agree, and confidence is above the 0.70 floor.

The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check was run because the deviation is material (13.76 km > 8.0 km): driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no repeat pattern is established, no POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift applies and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral issues. No other exculpatory route is open: the chat log is empty (POL-RD-04), no pickup or dropoff amendment exists (POL-RD-05), the fare is METERED not UPFRONT_QUOTE (POL-RD-11), and the vehicle is RYDE_TAXI not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12). No driver compensation is payable: the billed 51.9 km is not less than the trace's 51.86 km, so there is no unbilled-kilometre shortfall. The rider's personal remarks about the driver's questions at the end of the trip are carried by no artifact — the in-app chat log is empty — and no clause in this policy produces a referral on them; they can be raised with support separately.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.20 to the rider.

ruling.explanation:
Your trip from Woodlands MRT (Exit C) to Changi Airport Terminal 2 is a genuine and material route deviation, and a partial refund of SGD 13.20 is due to the rider.

MEASURED FACTS. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00513) records 51.86 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events; the platform's booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-00513) is 38.1 km. That is an excess of 13.76 km, or 36.1% over optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) and the excess is additionally material (greater than 8.0 km). Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs; the trip record's 51.9 km is a rounded convenience copy and was not used for the threshold test. The rider's recollection of 'fifty kilometres somehow became seventy' is not the measured figure — the excess is 13.76 km, not 20 km — but the refund is unaffected either way, because POL-RD-02 computes it from the optimal route, never from the actual distance.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXPLANATION. The assertion of a jam near Marina and an app re-route was tested, as POL-RD-13 requires, against the only advisory on file for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00513-01 (LTA DataMall ADV-20261413-001, slow traffic on the MCE westbound). Its validity window overlaps the trip, but its intersects_route flag is false — it covers a corridor the optimal route never uses — and its shortest_lawful_alternative_km is null, so the POL-RD-03 exoneration test (name a road the optimal route traverses; leave the corridor before the affected segment and rejoin after; compute the 130% cap) cannot be satisfied. POL-RD-03 states that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing, and under POL-RD-08 an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge the driver's burden. The excess therefore stands at the measured 13.76 km.

THE ALTERNATIVE ESCALATION ARGUMENT. The driver argued that POL-RD-10(5) is engaged because the advisory lacks the cap field, so the record cannot settle exoneration and the case must escalate. That is rejected. The advisory is on file at full weight (1.0) and its window covers the trip window, so this is not the POL-RD-10(5) case of an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact that is missing, window-missing, or field-less. The clause was available and was tested; it failed on its own first limb. A failed excuse is not a question the record cannot answer, and it does not escalate.

DRIVER-PROFILE CHECK (POL-RD-06), compulsory because the deviation is material. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in the same window — neither the 3-flag limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb is met. No repeat pattern is established, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift of the charged total and no driver-conduct referral. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two fields, and only those two were used.

THE REFUND ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02). recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 38.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 42.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge multiplier, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 44.935. Refund = charged total 58.09 minus 44.935 = 13.155, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 13.20. That is 22.6% of the amount charged, below the 90% share that would convert the outcome into a full refund, so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND. Nothing is added for pass-through lines: erp_gantries is empty and the ERP and toll totals are 0.00, and the airport surcharge is 0.00 — correctly so, since this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, and a surcharge on such a trip would itself be a billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4). POL-RD-09(1) in any event forbids stacking pass-through corrections on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. None is due. The distance charged (51.9 km) is not less than the trace distance (51.86 km), so the more-than-1.0 km unbilled-distance shortfall POL-RD-04 requires does not exist.

THE RIDER'S CLOSING REMARKS. The observations about the driver's questions at the end of the trip are not carried by any artifact — the in-app chat log (EV-CHAT-00513) is empty — and the rider does not rest the claim on them. No clause produces a referral on these facts: POL-RD-06(c) does not fire because no repeat pattern is established, and there is no billing-integrity failure to refer. The conduct concern is noted for the record but does not alter the money ruling.

OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.20. The charged total of 58.09 stands, 13.20 is returned to the rider, and the balance of 44.89 stands as the fare recomputed on the optimal route.

Refund before rounding is 13.155, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 13.20. That is 22.6% of the amount charged, far below the 90% that would convert this into a FULL_REFUND, so the ruling is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 13.20 and nothing else.

The rider's pleaded figures ('fifty kilometres somehow became seventy') are not the measured ones, and under POL-RD-01 the governing field is the trace, not the recollection. On EV-GPS-00513 the actual distance is 51.86 km against a booked optimal of 38.1 km, an excess of 13.76 km, or 36.1% — it clears both POL-RD-01 gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and is additionally MATERIAL (over 8.0 km), but it is 13.76 km, not the 20 km the claim asserts. The remedy cannot be inflated by the pleaded number: POL-RD-02's recomputed_fare depends only on optimal_distance_km and optimal_duration_min, never on the actual distance, so no larger deviation yields a larger refund.

The material deviation does trigger the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check, and that check comes back clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither limb of the pattern test is met (0 flags is below the 3-flag limb, and 0/250 = 0.00 is below the 0.05 ratio limb with more than 40 trips). No pattern being established, there is no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c); only the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 13.20 moves. Those two fields are the only ones POL-RD-06 names, and POL-GEN-01 confines the test to them.

Nothing is added to the POL-RD-02 figure for pass-through or statutory lines. The fare_breakdown shows erp_lines totalling 0.00 with no gantry charged, tolls_erp of 0.00, and airport_surcharge of 0.00 — correctly so, because this trip ENDS at Changi and a surcharge on an arriving trip would itself be a billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4). No off-route ERP was charged, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids stacking a pass-through correction on top of the POL-RD-02 refund in any event. The rider's total recovery is therefore SGD 13.20.

The driver's contemporaneous account — a jam near Marina and an app re-route — is corroborated as to the congestion by an independent third-party record: EV-ADVIS-00513-01 (LTA DataMall, ADV-20261413-001) logs slow traffic on the MCE corridor, active 06:16:40 to 08:16:40, overlapping this trip window by 52.0 minutes, which is exactly the Marina-area congestion the driver describes; the driver's profile carries no deviation flags. The driver does not, however, contend that POL-RD-03 exonerates him: that advisory's intersects_route flag is false and shortest_lawful_alternative_km is null, so it neither names a segment the optimal route traverses nor supplies the cap figure POL-RD-03 requires, and under POL-RD-13 an external-traffic assertion is tested against this advisory and nothing else. The excess therefore stands at the measured 13.76 km.

If the tribunal instead treats the driver's POL-RD-03 invocation as live, POL-RD-10(5) is engaged rather than answered: the exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact, EV-ADVIS-00513-01, that lacks the field the clause's cap requires — shortest_lawful_alternative_km is null, so 1.30 x (alternative - optimal) + 1.00 cannot be computed on this record and the record cannot say what part, if any, of the 13.76 km the advisory justifies. On that reading the record does not settle the exoneration question, and the mandatory outcome is ESCALATE: the disputed SGD 58.09 is held rather than collected or refunded while a human reviewer sees the case, the admissibility report and both briefs (POL-GEN-03).
